entries.title: Hakeem Jeffries’ Miami Trip Lands Cuban-Owned Bakery in Political Firestorm
entries.summary: The bakery later apologized for hosting the Democrats and denounced socialism.
entries.content:
A Cuban bakery in Florida has become the target of a conservative boycott campaign this week after it hosted a visit from House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and a Democratic congressional candidate.

Jeffries and Eliott Rodriguez, who is running in Florida’s 27th Congressional District, went to the bakery in Pinecrest, a Miami suburb, on Friday, meeting with one of the family business’s owners in what appeared to be a relatively routine campaign stop.

Rodriguez, who is Cuban-American, posted a video on social media of the visit while standing alongside CAO Bakery co-owner Yvette Cao. In the footage, Cao gives Jeffries a “care package” of pastries.

Jeffries thanked her for hosting them and thanked Rodriguez for his commitment to “making this community, making Florida and making the country more affordable.”

But the reception ignited a firestorm of backlash from the Miami Cuban community, many of whom accused the bakery of supporting “socialism” by hosting the Democrats — a touchy subject among the community of Cuban exiles who escaped the island nation’s communist government.

Several angry locals left comments on Rodriguez’s video stating they’d no longer patronize the business, while supporters said they’d exclusively purchase Cuban pastries from the bakery.

“I was a loyal Saturday morning customer until now,” wrote one commenter. “I will never set foot in any of your stores again.”

The backlash prompted an apology from Cao, who posted on the bakery’s Instagram account: “To the Cao community, I’ve read your messages and I understand why Friday hurts.”

She said hosting the candidates was not an endorsement.

“Cao stands with our Cuban American community for a free Cuba and condemns Socialism. That will never change,” she wrote.

Cao explained that Rodriguez’s campaign contacted the bakery the day before asking if they could stop by and greet the community.

“As a business, we don’t discriminate based on political views, but at the same time, I didn’t know it would turn into a press conference,” she said, adding: “Our family is here because of what our parents and grandparents gave up to be here. We know what they left behind, and everything we’ve built comes from the freedom this country gave us.”

Rodriguez’s opponent, Rep. María Elvira Salazar, posted about the controversy on X.

“Eliott Rodriguez brought the man who wants to lead the socialists in Congress into a Cuban bakery in Miami and, in one move, showed just how little he knows this community,” she wrote.

“He and his socialist friends turned a Cuban small business into a political prop and left the business dealing with the fallout. It is an insult to parade this ideology through a community built by survivors of socialism and embrace the very people who champion it.”

Polls have consistently shown there’s strong support for President Donald Trump in the Florida Cuban community.

That support handed Trump Miami-Dade County in the 2024 presidential election — the first time that it had flipped red since 1988.

Cuban restaurants and bakeries have long been places for politicians to campaign in Florida.

In June 2023, President Donald Trump stopped by Versailles in Little Havana. He was greeted by crowds of supporters who sang “Happy Birthday” to him.

entries.title: For All of Their Flaws, the Commanders Still Have Hope in the NFC East
entries.summary: Washington’s true identity seemed obvious during Monday night’s loss to the 49ers. Then the second half started.
entries.content:
By halftime of Monday night’s game at Levi’s Stadium, the Washington Commanders, for whatever else they were lacking, at least had established an identity. After an embarrassing, noncompetitive first half against the San Francisco 49ers, on top of five earlier games’ worth of incriminating evidence, they were now 30 minutes of football away from their bye week, and they were pretty much cooked.

Their season looked to be a washout. Their embattled coach seemed destined to be fired. They were nearing blow-it-up-and-start-over territory. For Commanders fans, that wasn’t much comfort. But at least there was now a sense of clarity. You could turn off your television at halftime, spare yourself the agony of whatever humiliation the second half had in store, and sleep peacefully with the hope that heads might soon start rolling on Coach Gibbs Drive.

But now, after a furious second-half comeback that saw the Commanders — with an astonishing, out-of-nowhere mixture of might and fight — put themselves in position to win a seemingly unwinnable game twice in the final six minutes, even that sense of clarity is gone. What in heaven’s name is the Commanders’ identity now?

Nothing that happened in Monday night’s second half has materially changed the trajectory of their season. They still lost, 23-17. They’re still a one-win team through six weeks. Their franchise quarterback, Jayden Daniels, is still winless in his four starts in 2026. They still make too many critical, boneheaded mistakes to be taken seriously. Oh, and on top of everything else, it looks as if they will be without the soul of their locker room, veteran wideout Terry McLaurin, for a long while following his first-quarter knee injury.

There are no moral victories in the NFL, right? Right?

And yet, it feels as if that second half changed everything.

The way Daniels carved up the 49ers’ defense on that fourth-quarter touchdown drive to make it a one-score game. … The way the Commanders’ defense forced San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy and mates into a pair of late three-and-outs. … The heart the entire team displayed in rallying from 20 points down on the road to put a serious scare into one of the best teams in the NFL, when the natural inclination may have been to pack it in at halftime. … Those 30 minutes of football may have just saved the Commanders’ season, not to mention coach Dan Quinn’s job.

At the very least, the Commanders’ true identity remains to be established. And that’s a good thing, right? Right?

Nobody is going to sit here and tell you this is a great team, or even a pretty good one. It also remains to be seen whether Quinn is the right coach for this moment, particularly after another massive mental breakdown in Monday night’s second quarter when, after Daniels inexplicably threw away a fourth-down pass attempt, Quinn appeared to have lost track of what down it was. (He would later say he knew the Commanders had turned the ball over on downs and was not calling for the field-goal unit, as internet lip-readers claimed.)

But one thing is certain: the NFC East is an historically bad division — one in which, for the first time in NFL history, the entire division just went winless in back-to-back weeks in which all four teams played. For all their problems, the Commanders (1-4-1) are just two games back of the division-leading New York Giants (3-2-1).

Ask yourself this: who is the most dangerous team in the NFC East right now? The first-place Giants (whom the Commanders should have beaten last week except for their inexplicable time-management meltdown on the final play of overtime) lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the rest of the season in Week 2, and the Philadelphia Eagles (2-4) just lost theirs, Jalen Hurts, also for the season. The Dallas Cowboys (2-4) have the 31st-ranked rushing offense and 32nd-ranked rushing defense in the NFL.

“We see the way the division is right now, the way things are going,” Sonny Styles, the Commanders’ rookie linebacker, told reporters Monday night. “We still have a chance. We’ve just got to keep fighting. [But] you’ve got to find a way to win at the end of the game.”

Anybody who studied the Commanders’ 2026 schedule when it first dropped in May understood the first half of it was going to be a gauntlet, with five of their first eight games coming against 2025 playoff teams. Through Week 6, it has been something close to a worst-case scenario. But their next two opponents — the Eagles (Nov. 1) and Los Angeles Rams (Nov. 8), both at home — are nowhere as scary as they looked last season, and the schedule eases considerably over the final two months.

There is, in other words, an argument to be made that the Commanders, so long as Daniels can stay on the field, are the most dangerous team in their division — an admittedly remarkable thing to say about a franchise that has won just three of its last 18 games dating to last October, with eight of those losses coming by double digits — or, at the very least, are as good as anyone else.

If Monday night’s second half accomplished nothing else, it may have bought them the opportunity to go out and prove it.

entries.title: Trump Is Cutting Right-Wing YouTuber Nick Shirley a Check for His Minnesota Video
entries.summary: Shirley is receiving $10,000 as part of a new fraud tipline rewards program.
entries.content:
The White House is announcing a new $25 million fraud tip program, to give Americans a cash reward for reporting suspected fraud that leads to a successful conviction or “significant federal enforcement action.”

Its first recipient: right-wing YouTuber Nick Shirley, whose viral December 2025 video resurfaced long-standing state and federal investigations into fraud at Somali-owned child care centers in Minnesota. The Trump administration promoted Shirley’s video, which in part jump-started its focus on fraud and led to punitive measures against the state.

The Trump administration is giving Shirley a $10,000 check as part of its new Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program.

Many of the administration's claims about fraud-related savings are misleading and unsubstantiated, as The Washington Sun has previously reported.

The state has indeed been dealing with a welfare fraud scandal centered on a nonprofit called Feeding Our Future, which exploited a child nutrition program during the pandemic. Aimee Bock, the woman at the center of that $250 million scheme, was sentenced to nearly 42 years in prison earlier this year. Investigations into the nonprofit predate Shirley’s video.

Minnesota state inspectors visited the child care centers featured in Shirley’s video after it went viral and found that they were operating normally. Fahima Mahamud, who led Future Leaders Early Learning Center, a day care featured in Shirley’s video, pleaded guilty to fraud charges related to the Feeding Our Futures scheme in July.

The administration’s new $25 million fraud tip program, administered by the Justice Department, will offer up to $30,000 to individuals who submit a tip to fraud.gov that leads to a successful conviction or “significant federal enforcement action.” It’s not immediately clear where that funding is coming from.

“Every day, President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud is zeroing in on the rampant abuse of taxpayer dollars and giving Americans the accountability they deserve,” White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said in a statement. “This administration has zero tolerance for individuals who steal from Americans.”

Minnesota has been a central focus of the administration’s campaign.

Late last year, the Minnesota Star Tribune tallied over $200 million in fraud documented by investigators in the state’s Education Department meal program and various Medicaid services.

Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz dropped out of the state’s gubernatorial race amid increased scrutiny at the start of this year.

Much of the administration’s rhetoric has focused on the Somali background of some of the fraudsters. Trump has repeatedly made racist comments about Minnesota’s Somali population. In a post on Truth Social earlier this month, he said the state “is being taken over by Somali Immigrants” and “the people of Minnesota must fight back.”

The Trump administration has taken a number of actions in response to Shirley’s video, including freezing child care payments to Minnesota and four other Democratic-run states and sending federal law enforcement to Minnesota to target immigrants. Earlier this year, federal law enforcement shot and killed two U.S. citizens protesting that crackdown.

The administration linked the surge of federal agents in Minneapolis earlier this year to the fraud scandal. Some federal prosecutors who’d been leading the sweeping pandemic fraud investigation in the state resigned after being asked to investigate the widow of Renée Good, one of the people shot and killed there.

State officials have accused the administration of politicizing fraud. The state is currently bracing for the Trump administration to officially withdraw up to $259 million in Medicaid payments that it froze earlier this year in the name of rooting out fraud.

entries.title: DCCC Jumps Into Three New House Races
entries.summary: The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee is adding spending, as it drops $16 million in coordinated TV ads in the second to last week of the campaign.
entries.content:
House Democrats are pouring money into three new congressional districts President Donald Trump won handily in 2024, pushing their party deeper into GOP territory in the final two weeks of 2026 cycle.

The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee is adding TV reservations in Arizona’s 2nd District, Ohio’s 10th District and South Carolina’s 1st District — two of which Trump won by double digits last election.

The additional buys are part of the committee’s $16 million coordinated TV ad campaign this week, the details of which were shared first with The Washington Sun. The DCCC is now spending, in coordination with Democratic candidates, in 49 House districts, two-thirds of which are currently held by Republicans.

The DCCC’s expansion reflects the shifting battlefield for the House this month, as Democrats go further on offense while Republicans cut defensive spending to at least two of their members. Republicans, weighed down by high gas prices and an unpopular president, are lagging behind Democrats in public and private polling. Democrats average a high single-digit lead in polling on the generic ballot.

Last week, the Congressional Leadership Fund, the super PAC aligned with GOP leadership, canceled its spending for Reps. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-Iowa) and Tom Kean Jr. (R-New Jersey). CLF also cut its efforts to take out a pair of Democratic incumbents representing districts Trump won in 2024, while retrenching cash into 16 Republican-held districts across the country.

In Arizona’s 2nd, where the DCCC is now spending, Rep. Eli Crane faces Jonathan Nez, the former Navajo Nation president, in a district Trump won by 15 percentage points two years ago. And in South Carolina’s 1st, Democrats are making a play for the seat left vacant by Rep. Nancy Mace, who ran an unsuccessful campaign for governor. Charleston County Council member Jenny Honeycutt, the GOP nominee for the seat, is facing Nancy Lacore, a retired Navy vice admiral, in a district Trump won by 13 percentage points.

In Ohio, where two hotly contested statewide races dominate spending, Democrats are now wading into Rep. Mike Turner’s race against Democrat Kristina Knickerbocker, a nurse and veteran. Trump won the seat by nearly 8 percentage points in 2024.

entries.title: AJ Dybantsa Ruled Out of Wizards’ Season Opener With an Ankle Injury
entries.summary: Coach Brian Keefe said the No.1 pick will remain day-to-day.
entries.content:
Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa will have to wait a bit longer before making his NBA debut after he was ruled out for Wednesday’s season opener with an ankle injury.

Wizards coach Brian Keefe said during a team practice Tuesday that the No. 1 pick will miss Wednesday’s meeting with the Bucks and remains day-to-day. Dybantsa sprained his left ankle during the second quarter of Friday’s preseason finale against the Pelicans.

After the Pelicans game, Keefe said pulling Dybantsa after his injury was precautionary and added that the team would “take it one day at a time” when asked whether Dybantsa would play against the Bucks.

On Tuesday, Keefe said Dybantsa was the only Wizards player ruled out for the opener.

entries.title: Judge Says Trump’s DOJ Can’t Get a Citizen Lawsuit Against xAI Dismissed
entries.summary: But the administration will be allowed to intervene in the case alleging an xAI data center violated the Clean Air Act.
entries.content:
The Justice Department will be allowed to intervene in a citizen lawsuit against xAI’s data center in Mississippi, but cannot throw the case out of court, a federal judge ruled Monday.

Lawyers for the Trump administration argued they had the right to unilaterally dismiss a lawsuit filed by the NAACP, which alleges that Elon Musk’s xAI violated the Clean Air Act and Mississippi state law by building and operating gas-fired generators without a permit to power a data center.

The Justice Department argued that the case should be dismissed for national security reasons and to align with federal policy and the public interest.

“Preserving xAI’s current data center capacity is a matter of paramount national security,” Cameron Stanley, chief digital and artificial intelligence officer at the Defense Department, said in a declaration as part of the case.

In Monday’s order, U.S. District Court Judge Debra Brown said she did not consider the national security concerns relevant to whether the Justice Department would be allowed to dismiss the case entirely.

Brown wrote that the Justice Department does not have the authority to unilaterally dismiss the lawsuit unless the federal or state government is already prosecuting the issue itself. That is not the case with xAI.

“It is readily apparent that by enacting the citizen suit provision, Congress intended to allow

individuals to sue even when federal and state governments may, for whatever reason, decline to enforce the Clean Air Act,” Brown wrote.

Despite denying the United States’ request to dismiss, Brown will allow the Justice Department to be part of the case going forward.

The NAACP is aiming to require that xAI operate its gas plant in compliance with the Clean Air Act and install emissions-control technology. The lawsuit also seeks to penalize the company up to $124,426 per day, per violation. The Justice Department and Mississippi Gov. Tate Reeves have said those penalties threaten the operation of xAI’s data center.

The judge asked lawyers for the Trump administration to explain the extent to which they will intervene by Friday.

Citizens have long been allowed to bring lawsuits over Clean Air Act violations. Those lawsuits have imposed penalties on companies including Exxon Mobil and U.S. Steel for emissions and permit violations.

The Defense Department relies on an xAI product known as the “Grok Gov Model,” Stanley said, which provides support for military operations as well as business enterprise activities. The agency used Grok to “deploy over 2,000 munitions to 2,000 distinct targets” during the U.S. campaign against Iran that killed Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei.

Users of the agency’s AI network consume almost 2 billion tokens — the units used to purchase AI model usage — every day, Stanley said.

The Justice Department also argued that allowing the lawsuit to move forward would compromise the enforcement authority of the federal government, placing it in the hands of citizens who sue.

entries.title: Rubio Says Ukraine Isn’t Being ‘Deliberately Denied’ Intelligence or Weapons
entries.summary: The secretary of state acknowledged intelligence problems this week, and missile deliveries may be awaiting Pentagon approval.
entries.content:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied Tuesday that the United States was deliberately withholding air defense missiles or intelligence from Ukraine, though he acknowledged that a shipment of Patriot interceptors purchased by European allies may be awaiting Pentagon approval.

Speaking to reporters in India after a phone call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Rubio said the U.S. faces competing demands for the sophisticated missiles, which are also needed to protect American military installations and allies around the world.

“There's nothing being deliberately denied to Ukraine,” Rubio said. “It's simply a balance between our obligations to other partners and, frankly, our own standards and requirements for our own facilities as well.”

Rubio was responding to complaints from Zelenskyy and U.S. lawmakers that delays in missile deliveries and disruptions in American intelligence sharing have left Ukrainian civilians vulnerable to Russian ballistic missile attacks.

Asked specifically about a batch of interceptors purchased by European countries under the Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List, or PURL, that reportedly requires Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s sign-off, Rubio did not rule out that the shipment was being held up.

“These things are always reviewed through the context of whether they're needed somewhere else or whether they even need to remain in Europe,” Rubio said. “We do have bases in Europe. Our partners do as well.”

The Washington Post reported Monday that the Trump administration had not approved interceptors from countries seeking to provide them to Ukraine. Those transfers require approval because the interceptors are American made. Reuters reported separately that Hegseth had not authorized delivery of the latest weapons package purchased by NATO allies through PURL.

The Pentagon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Patriot interceptors, already in demand in Europe in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, have become highly sought around the globe — including by the United States as it grapples with stockpiles diminished in the Iran war. The Trump administration has been pushing to ramp up production of the complex weapons, but it may take years for those efforts to turn into new deliveries.

Rubio said the U.S. is juggling commitments to Ukraine, Israel and Saudi Arabia with its own requirements to protect U.S. installations.

“Every country in the world would like interceptors, and many parts of the world are asking for that,” he said. “So, when a country doesn't get interceptors from the United States, it's not because they’re being denied. We have our own needs too.”

Relations between President Donald Trump and Zelenskyy are under intense strain after Trump’s recent rejection of new Russia sanctions and after Kyiv experienced disruptions in U.S. satellite support for its drones during the war.

Rubio said Trump has been “angry and frustrated” by a lack of progress toward a negotiated settlement and by suggestions that he is deliberately undermining Ukraine’s defenses. He also acknowledged Trump’s objections to Ukraine’s strikes on Russian energy infrastructure due to their impact on global markets.

“The president, more than anything, is responding to the insinuation that somehow he is doing things to deliberately harm Ukraine, which is not fair and not true,” Rubio said.

Rubio forcefully denied the administration had curbed the intelligence sharing with Ukraine that warns it of incoming missile attacks.

“The president made it very clear he’s ordered no such changes,” Rubio said. “None of that has changed.”

Rubio acknowledged Ukraine may have experienced problems receiving or acting on intelligence on Oct. 13 and 18, but said it was either an “internal issue” or a “technical” matter.

“I saw somebody associated with the Ukrainian government say that people in Ukraine are dying because the U.S. is denying information,” he said. “That's scandalous. That's outrageous. That's just simply not true.”

Zelenskyy has talked with American lawmakers about worsening problems with Ukraine’s air defenses as well as the interceptor delivery delays.

“We should be doing everything we can to help Ukraine defend its cities,” said Rep. Don Bacon (R-Nebraska), who told The Washington Sun that Zelenskyy discussed the delays in a call with him on Monday. “I’d pull from our own inventory, and I’d coordinate with other countries to do the same. Trump is trying to impede other countries from helping. It’s an immoral policy.”

Sens. Richard Blumenthal (D-Connecticut) and Thom Tillis (R-North Carolina) said Zelenskyy reported disruptions in early-warning intelligence as well as ongoing restrictions on Starlink and Starshield satellite communications.

“As a result of these disruptions, civilians — children — are dying,” the senators wrote in a joint statement.

Ukraine has been pressing Washington for months to speed up Patriot interceptor deliveries, particularly as Russia targets its energy facilities and ahead of the winter.

In August, former Vice President Mike Pence said on CNN that Zelenskyy had asked whether the United States could spare roughly 5% of its remaining Patriot interceptors to help Ukraine defend itself through the winter.

entries.title: Trump Administration Takes Another Swing at California’s Medicaid Program
entries.summary: Mehmet Oz announced the government is freezing $1.2 billion in federal Medicaid payments to the state.
entries.content:
The Trump administration is freezing $1.2 billion in federal Medicaid payments to California, its largest deferral yet as it targets the state’s in-home care program over fraud allegations.

Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Administrator Mehmet Oz announced the deferral Tuesday during an event with President Donald Trump.

CMS has already withheld an unprecedented sum — around $2.2 billion — from the state over the course of this year. Most of those funds were for California’s In-Home Supportive Services program, which compensates family members and other caregivers for helping patients with tasks like washing, dressing and feeding themselves.

The Trump administration alleges the program is riddled with fraud, pointing in part to the program’s rapid growth in recent years. California has protested the deferrals, saying the federal government hasn’t provided it with sufficient evidence of fraud and that growth is a function of ballooning demand.

“California has been growing that program 24% in the last three years,” Oz said Tuesday. “That is twice the rate of every other state average in the country. Impossible for us to understand how that could be so.”

Oz also repeated a suggestion he’s made several times before: that the state is paying caregivers to provide services that family members would otherwise take care of.

“Many of you would carry groceries upstairs for your mom for free, I would think, but in California they'll pay you a lot of money for it,” Oz said.

Neither CMS nor California state officials immediately responded to a request for comment.

The administration has made fighting fraud a central message ahead of the November midterm elections. Vice President JD Vance and members of his anti-fraud task force have touted actions in Medicaid, the individual health insurance marketplaces and the food stamp program, saying they’re shoring up federal safety programs for the Americans who qualify for them.

The funds deferred to California total around 4% of its annual federal payments for Medicaid, which is a program run by states and partially funded by the federal government.

Besides California, CMS has also deferred Medicaid payments to Minnesota over fraud allegations. The deferred funds are under review by CMS, which could decide to pay them or cancel them entirely. The states would be on the hook to make up any of those payments.

entries.title: Susan Collins’ New Strategy: Sounding a Lot Like Her Democratic Opponent
entries.summary: The Republican is making the case that her seniority is the difference-maker for voters in Maine.
entries.content:
Maine Sen. Susan Collins has been deploying a rare tactic in a battleground Senate race: agreeing with her opponent.

“Troy [Jackson] and I agree that the war should come to an end ... I agree that the president did not have a good plan,” she said of the war in Iran.

“Both of us would have voted no on final passage,” she said of Republicans’ 2025 reconciliation package.

“The bottom line is that Troy and I both would have voted against the Canadian tariffs,” she said of President Donald Trump’s trade dispute.

Collins made those comments during a debate against Troy Jackson, her Democratic opponent. Collins is arguing to voters that the biggest difference between her and Jackson is that her seniority, particularly on the Senate Appropriations Committee, and position as a key Republican vote give her the power to spare Maine from more dramatic effects of Trump’s agenda.

“There’s a fundamental difference between Senator Collins and Troy Jackson: she delivers results; he would get nothing,” Blake Kernen, the communications director for the Collins campaign, said in a statement to The Washington Sun.

Jackson, meanwhile, argues that a reliable Democratic vote would benefit Maine more.

“Unlike Collins, Troy would not have voted to confirm Brett Kavanaugh, advance legislation slashing Mainers’ health care, or hand ICE billions without guardrails. Those votes have real consequences for people who can’t afford a lobbyist in Washington,” said Maggie Amjad, a spokesperson for Jackson, in a statement to The Sun.

“Thirty years of seniority means nothing to a family losing health care or struggling to heat their home,” she said. “What matters is whose side you’re on.”

When Collins started her first term in 1997, Republicans made up half of New England’s Senate delegation. Now she’s the only one, and widely seen as the only Republican capable of winning a Senate seat in Maine. She’s also the only Republican senator in the country running for reelection in a state that Kamala Harris won in 2024.

Collins, who is often critical of Trump, is running on a personal record of being able to secure funding for projects across the state, emphasizing the constituent work she’s spent years doing from Washington.

“It is a very hard job to try to shoehorn in a one-size-fits-all policy across every part of this state, but Susan Collins does it better than anybody else that I have ever seen,” said Maine state Senate Minority Leader Trey Stewart, a Republican backing Collins, adding that the state is “wicked diverse,” with competing interests in the logging, fishing, farming, shipbuilding and tourism industries.

Trump has never won statewide in Maine, but some of his policies are having outsize effects there, including the U.S.-Canada trade dispute — since Maine is a border state — and immigration enforcement — an ICE agent shot and killed a Colombian man in Biddeford.

Matthew Bartlett, a Republican strategist and former Trump appointee, told The Sun that the race is about who can be a more effective voice against the president, especially as his poll numbers reach all-time lows.

“There aren’t many people that are looking for a MAGA warrior in these midterms, much less in Maine,” Bartlett said. “There’s some credibility she has — not many people mistake Susan Collins for Donald Trump.”

Trump has lashed out at her repeatedly. When asked at a debate if Trump would hold a rally for her in Maine, Collins said that she’s “not exactly his favorite senator” and he wouldn’t be visiting. And after she voted to pass a War Powers Resolution aimed at curbing his power to expand military operations in Venezuela, he included her on a list of senators he said “should never be elected to office again.”

entries.title: Ohio's Amy Acton Condemns Attack Ad Featuring Her Estranged Mother
entries.summary: The ad aimed at the gubernatorial candidate began circulating on social media Monday evening and does not include a disclaimer of who paid for it.
entries.content:
Amy Acton, Ohio’s Democratic gubernatorial candidate, denounced an attack ad Tuesday that features her estranged mother, who was married to a man accused of sexually abusing Acton when she was a child.

The ad, which does not include a disclaimer about who paid for it, began appearing on social media Monday evening. Acton’s mother, Donna Arthur, reportedly sided with Acton’s stepfather, Cledith Arthur, after he was charged with raping Acton when Acton was still a child. Cledith Arthur died in 2004.

“I won’t normalize somebody who has said that my childhood is something I’m just complaining about, who today just released an ad using my birth mother who I was removed from at the age of 12 for severe abuse and neglect,” Acton said in a clip of an appearance on Spectrum News that was posted to social media.

She blamed her Republican opponent, Vivek Ramaswamy, for the ad and framed it as part of a broader trend, reminiscent of Ramaswamy’s comments during the GOP presidential primary debates in 2023 when he was a candidate. In one debate, Ramaswamy targeted Nikki Haley’s daughter for using TikTok after Haley had criticized Ramaswamy for using the app.

“This is a lifelong pattern with my opponent,” Acton said in a clip.

In campaign videos, Acton has described a childhood marked by homelessness and sexual abuse. She and her mother have both said they have not seen each other in nearly 50 years; the last time was the day Acton appeared in court after her stepfather was charged.

Donna Arthur in the ad says that Acton is a “liar” who would make the lives of Ohioans “worse.” While she does not address Acton’s allegations of sexual abuse, she says that Acton lied about experiencing homelessness.

"She lies about her past. She says she grew up living in a tent,” Donna Arthur said. “None of that is true, she's lied her entire life. My daughter needs help."

A statement from the Ramaswamy campaign did not address the ad’s origins.

“We don't know what happened between Amy and her mother, who first spoke out about Amy in 2020, but we know that Amy Acton is a serial fabulist who has some serious problems with the truth that the public needs to be aware of before deciding who to entrust as governor,” campaign spokesperson Connie Luck said in a statement provided to The Washington Sun.

Polling has been split in the high-profile race for governor, but the race has trended in Acton’s favor in recent weeks. A Marist Poll released Tuesday found Acton leading Ramaswamy by 7 percentage points, while a New York Times poll from Oct. 4 placed the lead at around 4 percentage points.

In a video of a campaign speech posted to Ramaswamy’s social media earlier this year, Ramaswamy called on Ohio voters to elect someone with “a positive vision for our state, versus a governor who has none at all other than to complain about what someone else did to her.”

Acton’s campaign released a statement by her brother, Philip Stearns, calling the new ad a "despicable low” for Ramaswamy.

“To attempt to turn the sexual abuse Amy endured at twelve years old from our birth mother’s husband into a political talking point,” Stearns said. “This desperate, disgusting attack reveals exactly who Vivek Ramaswamy is at his core — a pathetic excuse for a man who is willing to hurt anyone as long as it gets him what he wants.”

entries.title: Trump Gives Conflicting Information on the Administration’s New Fraud Tip Program
entries.summary: The president said he will be the arbiter of who gets the awards. The Justice Department says it’s in charge.
entries.content:
President Donald Trump told reporters Tuesday that he himself would decide who gets a payout from his administration’s new rewards program for people who submit tips about fraud to the government. That’s not what the Justice Department said.

“I will be the arbitrator of all of these decisions,” Trump said. “In other words, I'll determine whether or not the person is deserving.”

The Justice Department, meanwhile, said that awards will be made “in the Justice Department’s sole discretion following the filing of criminal charges.”

The first recipient of money from the $25 million program is right-wing YouTuber Nick Shirley, whose viral 2025 video purporting to find day care fraud in Minnesota supercharged the administration’s fraud focus. The administration says that tipsters whose information leads to a successful conviction or “significant federal enforcement action” can get up to $30,000.

The president said that if there was a dispute over multiple people wanting the payout, he himself would make the call. “I'm not doing it for any other reasons other than to expedite because I think it's very important,” he said.

A DOJ FAQ page addresses that exact situation, saying that there can be more than one whistleblower, but each has to provide separate, original and nonpublic information. If the tips are the same, whoever submitted it first would get the reward.

Who decides awards recipients isn’t the only point of confusion. The White House says that the Justice Department is running the new tip program, but the website promoting the program says that the tips go to the Treasury Department for review.

A DOJ spokesperson told The Washington Sun that the funding for the program comes from Treasury, but the DOJ is managing the program. The DOJ said that the program is meant to encourage whistleblowers to report potential tips sooner by paying them out after charges are unsealed — not after final resolution of a criminal matter, like other tip programs.

Trump said that tips could be submitted through fraud.gov. When the program was announced the intake was housed on America.gov, the Trump administration’s AI-driven clearinghouse for government services.

The administration launched America.gov with fanfare last month, saying that it would help Americans access government benefits and services more easily using its AI chatbot.

entries.title: Dulles International Airport Moves VIP Terminal Plans Ahead
entries.summary: The terminal will include parking, private security screenings, suites, lounges and transport directly to planes.
entries.content:
A premium passenger terminal is coming to Washington Dulles International Airport where VIPs can enjoy some of the on-the-ground luxuries of flying private, even if they're commercial passengers.

The Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority, the body that oversees Dulles and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, released new details of the $125 million project Tuesday. The VIP terminal will offer customers, who will pay a yet-to-be-named price, dedicated parking, private security screenings, suites, lounges, bag handling services and vehicle transport directly to their aircrafts.

“By introducing this premium service, Dulles is responding to traveler demand, supporting continued growth and joining other leading international airports around the world that offer elevated services for business and leisure travelers alike,” Chryssa Westerlund, the airport authority’s executive vice president, said in a statement Tuesday.

The 37,000-square-foot facility will sit near the airport’s cargo buildings on a 1.2-acre site. An airport authority spokesperson told The Washington Sun that construction will not affect access to existing passenger areas at the airport.

The Metropolitan Airport Authority has talked about adding a VIP facility since 2023. It started accepting proposals from companies interested in building and managing the project in September 2025 before selecting Irish airport management company daa International to oversee it this summer.

Construction is planned to take about 30 months. It is unclear when work will start. Once the terminal is open, daa International will operate and manage it for an initial 20-year term.

The company has developed and operated VIP terminals before, including at the Dublin Airport and a terminal currently being designed in Vietnam.

“Washington Dulles International Airport plays a vital role in connecting the United States with the world, and we look forward to bringing our international airport experience and operational expertise to the delivery of a VIP facility that reflects the airport’s global standing,” daa International CEO Nick Cole said in a Tuesday statement. 

President Donald Trump has drilled into Dulles during his second term, calling the current terminals “disasters” and the airport “a terrible place to be.” He announced a $22 billion renovation project earlier this year.

entries.title: The FBI Was Reportedly Eyeing Graham and Clyburn as Part of a Bribery Probe
entries.summary: A ProPublica report claims the lawmakers put a company up for government contracts after receiving large campaign contributions.
entries.content:
The FBI was poised to investigate the late South Carolina Sen. Lindsey Graham and Rep. James Clyburn before President Donald Trump took office and barred the Justice Department’s anti-corruption section from pursuing new cases.

The department was probing a meeting between Graham and Martin Kao, the chief executive of Navatek, a marine defense research and development company, according to a report from ProPublica published Tuesday. It was also looking into what the investigative nonprofit called an alleged “cash-for-contacts” deal between Navatek and Clyburn, an influential Democratic power broker.

The allegations against Graham stemmed from a 2020 dinner that he agreed to attend for 45 minutes if Kao committed $40,000 in campaign contributions, the outlet reported.

At the meeting, Graham agreed to direct a $10 million government contract toward the company. During the face-to-face, Kao also pledged a total of $100,000 to his reelection campaign, according to ProPublica.

The FBI opened a bribery investigation in 2025, with Graham’s dinner as a main focal point, the outlet reported. However, the investigation went cold after Trump was sworn in and effectively disbanded the DOJ team handling public corruption.

Kao told federal agents he bribed lawmakers on both sides of the aisle, including Clyburn and Rep. Joe Wilson (R-South Carolina).

The agency did not consider Graham, Clyburn or Wilson subjects of the investigation, but FBI agents indicated they could be subjects in the future, ProPublica reported. Two men the FBI did consider subjects, Navatek executives Duke Hartman and Joshua Knight, were never charged.

Last year, Kao was sentenced to 87 months in prison after he pleaded guilty to a loan fraud scheme in 2022.

A representative for Graham denied the allegations in a statement to ProPublica, calling them the “ravings of a convicted felon” and “simply false.”

A representative for Clyburn also dismissed the story.

“Whatever a donor may think or say, a donation would never cause Congressman Clyburn to increase his support for the donor’s request,” Jami LaRue, Clyburn’s communications director, told ProPublica.

Kao’s business model boiled down to bribing public officials in exchange for contracts, he told the FBI, according to documents reviewed by ProPublica. Kao admitted the research his company provided for the government was “often worthless.”

Kao told ProPublica from prison that what he participated in was “corruption at its best.”

The Washington Sun emailed representatives for Graham, Clyburn and Wilson for comment.

The company first began approaching lawmakers in 2019. The next year, Navatek won $40.7 million in government contracts.

That same year, Wilson, Graham and Clyburn each asked for $100,000. Graham had a more direct approach, said Kao, according to the outlet.

“This is how much I want, and how much I am going to give you,” he recalled the lawmaker saying.

Navatek is no longer doing business under that name. Graham died in July at the age of 71.

Clyburn, 86, announced he’d be seeking reelection in March. Meanwhile, Wilson continues to serve as a senior member of the Armed Services Committee.

The Tuesday report follows an investigation by ProPublica last month that found Republican Sen. Susan Collins of Maine similarly pushed millions in government funding in Navatek’s direction while Navatek donated to her campaign. Collins denied any allegations of wrongdoing, ProPublica reported, and she called Kao a “convicted liar.”

entries.title: Michael Bloomberg Delivers $80 Million to Democrats in Final Midterms Stretch
entries.summary: Most of the cash influx will focus on House races, Bloomberg's team told The New York Times.
entries.content:
Democratic megadonor and former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg announced an $80 million funding influx to help his party chip away at a Republican financial advantage in the run up to the midterms.

Bloomberg’s team announced the hefty donation drop, which began September, in an interview published Tuesday in The New York Times. The last-minute cash flow isn’t anything new for the political benefactor who often significantly boosts his spending for Democrats in the last stretch of an election cycle.

“He believes in participation in our democracy,” Howard Wolfson, Bloomberg’s political adviser, told the Times.

Up to $50 million, which is more than half of Bloomberg’s reported spend, is heading to House races. With election forecasters predicting Democrats are on target to win back control of the House, some donors have refocused their attention on competitive Senate races across the country — but Bloomberg wants Democrats to have a comfortable majority in the lower chamber.

“The difference between 221 and 230, in terms of the House majority, really matters,” Wolfson said in the interview.

Everytown for Gun Safety, an organization Bloomberg co-founded, is set to receive $24 million; around $16 million is headed for the House Majority PAC, which is the super PAC tied to House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries.

Everytown for Gun Safety helped launch a $10 million ad campaign promoting former gun safety advocates now running for the House, Axios reported earlier this month.

But high-dollar spends do not always translate to success. Bloomberg failed to earn the Democratic nomination for president in 2020 despite spending more than $1 billion ahead of the primaries, significantly more than many of his Democratic opponents.

Undeterred, Bloomberg “is of the view that resources matter in campaigns,” Wolfson told the Times.

Republican Party committees had more than a $100 million cash on hand advantage over their Democratic counterparts, according to Federal Election Commission data through Aug. 31, though new monthly reports due Tuesday will account for September’s totals.

Wolfson told the Times that Bloomberg is not “directing” the funding push toward any recipients who represent the party’s left flank and support the Democratic Socialists of America — a group that has backed more progressive candidates this primary cycle and who have been responsible for major upsets to the Democratic establishment. Bloomberg, Wolfson said, is concerned about the Democratic Party’s position on Israel, and DSA and its candidates often advocate for Palestinian rights in the region and are strongly against increasing U.S. military aid to Israel.

Bloomberg has not made a decision on whom to support for the Democrats’ 2028 presidential primary, a race he is likely to shape with the help of his megadonor status.

“He is a pragmatist. He is a centrist,” Wolfson told the Times. “I would be surprised if in the end he didn’t support someone who shared that orientation and was from that wing of the party.”

entries.title: Commanders’ Terry McLaurin Will Miss the Rest of the Season
entries.summary: The veteran wide receiver tore his patellar tendon Monday night against the 49ers.
entries.content:
Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin will miss the rest of the season with a torn patellar tendon, coach Dan Quinn said on Tuesday. The 31-year-old is expected to undergo surgery.

McLaurin was carted off the field in the first quarter of the team’s “Monday Night Football” game against the 49ers. He appeared to get his feet tangled with San Francisco corner Deommodore Lenoir on a third-down route. McLaurin reached for his left leg as he fell to the ground and stayed down for some time as trainers provided an air cast.

After the game, Quinn said the team feared McLaurin’s injury was “significant,” and an MRI later showed that McLaurin needed surgery.

The veteran wideout was in his second game back after sitting out Week 4 with a hamstring injury. He missed seven games last season with a quad strain after not missing a single contest between 2021 and 2024. He will finish his 2026 season with 15 catches for 230 yards and a touchdown.

entries.title: Trump Administration Gives Farmers More Relief Ahead of Midterms
entries.summary: Republicans have grown increasingly concerned about losing races in deep-red states with rural voters.
entries.content:
President Donald Trump announced $8 billion in relief this harvest season for farmers facing record-high diesel prices, during a rally in Kansas to support vulnerable incumbent Republican Sen. Roger Marshall.

“Roger got it to happen. Good job, Roger,” Trump said. “And when the Republicans win, we will pass even more funding for our farmers. We love our farmers."

The Agriculture Department said the Farm Service Agency will administer one-time payments to farmers under its new Harvest Fuel Relief program and in November will announce rates for dairy, sugar and other commodities including major grain, oilseed and pulse crops.

The USDA did not announce when farmers can apply or when payments will go out.

“President Trump hears our farmers — and he is taking action,” Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said on X, highlighting several other recent moves the administration is undertaking to help farmers, including new fertilizer facilities and trade deals.

The relief comes as Republicans grow increasingly concerned about losing midterm races in deep-red states with rural voters, including Kansas and Nebraska. The announcement is also the second attempt this month to aid farmers facing high diesel prices, with Trump announcing expanded access to red-dyed diesel and a review of certain federal taxes.

Diesel fuel prices have reached record high prices largely because of the ongoing war with Iran. The increase has upset farmers and created competitive races in areas where Trump won by double digits just two years ago.

Marshall is in a tight race with Democrat Adam Hamilton in a state that hasn't elected a Democratic senator since 1932. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to win control of the Senate.

Zippy Duvall, president of the American Farm Bureau Federation, said in a statement that farmers and ranchers welcomed the announcement. “We appreciate President Trump and Secretary Rollins recognizing that higher diesel prices have squeezed farmers’ bottom lines,” Duvall said.

Other farm groups weren’t as quick to praise the administration, with some blaming it for diesel prices reaching this point in the first place.

“Farmers never should have been put in this position. A Band-Aid response now, 2 weeks before the election, doesn’t fix the problem,” Iowa Farmers Union President Aaron Lehman said in a statement.

Lehman said the harvest is already well underway, and farmers have already borne the brunt of high diesel prices, even if they end up getting money back.

“Farmers have been dumping expensive diesel fuel in their combines and tractors for weeks,” Lehman told The Washington Sun. “Farmers have been put in a situation because of bad policy decisions.”

entries.title: CNN Vows Further Legal Action if Air Force One Ban Continues
entries.summary: The network’s attorney said CNN has been blocked from traveling on the aircraft at least four times since Trump announced his initial press ban.
entries.content:
CNN warned the Justice Department on Monday that the network may pursue additional legal action if the Trump administration continues to ban the network’s journalists from traveling with the president aboard Air Force One.

CNN, MS NOW and Politico are locked in a legal battle to restore their access to the White House after President Donald Trump banned the outlets on Sept. 18. The new legal threat comes a week after a federal judge extended the preliminary injunction blocking the administration from barring the outlets’ reporters from White House grounds while the lawsuit proceeds.

The Trump administration has continued to restrict CNN’s access to Air Force One, which is the official call sign for any U.S. Air Force aircraft carrying the president. The outlet contends that blocking CNN from traveling with the president greatly affects the network’s ability to fulfill its duties as the rotating representative of the White House television pool — a group of TV networks that have an agreement to share information and resources while covering the president each day.

In a letter sent to the Justice Department, CNN attorney Theodore Boutrous demanded written confirmation by 5 p.m. Thursday that the Trump administration will cease all restrictions on CNN access to the Oval Office and Air Force One.

“If these actions persist, CNN will have no choice but to return to the court to defend its rights, and it is prepared to fight as long as is necessary to secure them,” Boutrous wrote in the letter dated Monday.

CNN has been denied access to the aircraft at least four times, Boutrous said, including during Trump’s trip to New York for the United Nations General Assembly on Sept. 21 and as recently as Friday, when the network learned it would be excluded from traveling with the president to Georgia and Florida. The White House has not provided the network with any written notice or explanation for the denials, the letter said.

Politico, which is also represented by Boutrous, has also been denied access to Air Force One at least one time, preventing the outlet from serving as the primary print pooler on Oct. 5.

Boutrous argued that the Trump administration is continuing to “retaliate and discriminate against CNN based on the content of its news coverage,” but the White House has repeatedly pushed back on the notion that news outlets have an absolute right to access.

“No person and no journalist has a constitutional right to access to the President’s Oval Office, Air Force One, or other sensitive and private facilities,” a White House official wrote in a statement to The Washington Sun. “When publications lie, fabricate, and ignore the truth, proximity matters less and they can write their fiction from outside of these secure facilities.”

The Justice Department declined to comment, citing ongoing litigation.

CNN’s letter says that traveling on Air Force One has become an essential part of covering Trump because he often hosts impromptu press gaggles while aboard the aircraft and on the tarmac.

“Through September of this year, the President has appeared in the White House Briefing Room only 4 times and taken approximately 96 questions there. During the same time period, he has held 43 press events in the Oval Office where he fielded at least 741 questions. Aboard Air Force One and on the tarmac, President Trump has made himself available to the press 51 times and fielded no fewer than 865 questions,” Boutrous wrote.

CNN has argued in court and in the letter that restrictions on the network's ability to cover Trump have profound effects on the American public’s access to the president because CNN is part of a broader pool agreement between five television networks.

“CNN has invested significant financial and other resources to ensure the highest quality television pool coverage of the President, whether he is in the White House or traveling across the country or overseas — pool coverage that reaches millions of Americans as well as viewers across the globe,” Boutrous wrote. “Preventing CNN from performing its full White House Television Pool duties deprives the American public of a vital source of information about the President and his activities.”

entries.title: James Talarico Campaign to Super PACs: Highlight Anti-Paxton Republicans
entries.summary: The Texas Democrat is using a controversial messaging technique known as “red-boxing” in an apparent attempt to avoid coordination restrictions.
entries.content:
Democrat James Talarico’s campaign has new marching orders for supportive super PACs during the final days of Texas’ Senate race: highlight Republicans who can’t stand Ken Paxton, his opponent.

And pro-Talarico PAC Lone Star Rising appeared to quickly heed the Talarico campaign’s request: On Tuesday, it ran an online advertisement featuring a woman named Erin, who identified herself as a longtime Republican that’s previously voted for President Donald Trump and Paxton.

“I didn’t care for [Paxton] personally, but I figured that didn’t matter. I was wrong,” Erin says in the ad. “Being Republican means being tough on crime. Ken Paxton offered a child sex abuser with ties to his rich friends one day in jail.”

“As a Republican, that makes me sick,” she continues. “As a mom, I’ll never get past it.”

Lone Star Rising appears to have taken its cue from an Oct. 13 message Talarico’s campaign posted on its “What Voters Need to Know About James” web page. It included directions to highlight the statement: “Ken Paxton’s corruption led to an admitted pedophile being offered one day in jail.”
Ken.Paxton.Trump (2576x1717, AR: 1.50)The message also suggested two groups in particular to target — “Non-MAGA Republicans” and independents. Those voters, the campaign wrote, “need to hear on digital, streaming and radio that Ken Paxton is too corrupt, even for life-long Republicans and Trump voters.”

For several months, the Talarico campaign has used this page to share preferred talking points that outside political groups may use in their own advertising — a practice known as “red-boxing” — without illegally coordinating with Talarico.

Along with “ordinary Republican voters,” the Talarico campaign wrote on the web page that conservative-leaning Texans should hear from “current and former GOP elected officials.”

The Talarico campaign specifically names Sen. John Cornyn, the outgoing Texas Republican Paxton narrowly defeated in their May runoff, and former Republican Rep. Louie Gohmert of Texas. It also names David Maxwell, who blew the whistle on Paxton for allegedly using his office to help a donor and has since endorsed Talarico.

The PAC, Lone Star Rising, did not respond to a request for comment. Lone Star Rising similarly ran ads mirroring the campaign’s public guidance earlier this year.

The Talarico campaign did not respond to The Washington Sun’s request for comment.

Throughout the campaign, Talarico has focused on billionaires imposing their will on elections as he seeks to become the first Democrat elected in Texas to statewide office in more than 30 years. At a CNN town hall last week, Talarico again touted his rejection of corporate PACs, saying that they should be banned.

While not illegal, campaign finance watchdogs have questioned the ethics of candidates releasing talking points via “red-boxing.” Super PACs, legally, cannot directly coordinate with candidates.

“Red-boxing” has become increasingly prevalent, especially this cycle among Democrats. During the 2024 election, more than 200 federal campaigns used the tactic, according to the Campaign Legal Center.

“James Talarico spent his entire campaign lecturing Texans about dark money and refusing corporate PAC dollars,” Paxton campaign spokesperson Madison Cercy told The Sun. “Now he’s posting talking points on his own website so super PACs know exactly what to say for him.”

Cercy also highlighted Reid Hoffman, a co-founder of LinkedIn who is financially backing Lone Star Rising. Hoffman has contributed $11.5 million to the group’s efforts as of Sept. 30, according to Federal Election Commission filings.

Paxton repeatedly questioned Cornyn’s conservative bona fides during their Republican primary earlier this year, eventually nabbing the president’s endorsement. Since then, Cornyn has not endorsed Paxton and has repeatedly sniped at him, although he’s said he’ll support the Republican ticket in Texas.
John Cornyn AP - 26146448513183 (5472x3648, AR: 1.50)Cornyn is “clearly not helping,” Paxton said at a fundraiser in September, according to audio obtained by CNN. “He wants me to lose.”

Cornyn’s office did not respond to a request for comment on the Talarico campaign seemingly elevating the senator in the final stretch of the campaign.

Trump wrote on Truth Social last week that Cornyn and GOP strategist Karl Rove were sabotaging Paxton.

“If Ken Paxton loses, it will be because of WEAK and INEFFECTIVE Political Hacks like John Cornyn and Karl Rove, who have ineffectively opposed me for my entire political career,” Trump said on his social media platform.

entries.title: DHS Plane Purchases Tied to ‘Ongoing Criminal Law Enforcement Investigation’
entries.summary: The department, while under Kristi Noem’s leadership, bought several aircraft over market value from a donor to a Noem-linked super PAC.
entries.content:
The purchase of several aircraft by the Department of Homeland Security during the final days of former Secretary Kristi Noem’s tenure is tied to an “ongoing criminal law enforcement investigation,” the department’s Privacy Office told The Washington Sun.

The acknowledgement, made as part of the department’s denial of an Oct. 14 Freedom of Information Act request, added that “DHS can neither confirm nor deny the existence of records responsive to this portion of the request. Confirming or denying the existence of such records could reasonably be expected to interfere with ongoing or prospective enforcement proceedings.”

The FBI and White House both referred a request for comment to DHS, which did not immediately return a request for comment. The Department of Justice did not immediately return a request for comment.

Earlier this month, Noem came under renewed scrutiny after The New York Times reported that DHS purchased five airplanes from a political donor, Daedalus Aviation Corporation, at a “substantial markup.”

President Donald Trump announced Noem’s firing on March 5 following a number of controversies that dogged her tenure at the department. Trump replaced her with then-Sen. Markwayne Mullin.

Noem took to social media after the Times story: “I write to formally request the retraction entirely or explicit correction of the article titled 'Kristi Noem’s Agency Gave Her Donor a Lucrative Contract Just Before She Left.'”

She also disputed the characterization of Daedalus as a political donor. Daedalus’ chair is William Walters, who gave $10,000 to the American Resolve political action committee, a super PAC that exists to help Noem.

The planes bought at the end of her tenure were bought above market value, according to the Times.

The Sun’s FOIA request asks for several sets of government records, including the agency’s acquisition decision memo for the seven Boeing 737-700 aircraft and one Gulfstream G650 acquired in or around December 2025, complete with seller, price, tail numbers and source of funds.

Also requested: purchase agreements, bills of sale, reimbursement records, flight data documents and policy documents or memos governing the use of the aircraft by senior officials.

At least some of the requested records appear to exist, as they are referenced by name in an agency filing posted to a government contracting site.

The Times similarly requested documents related to the planes’ purchases but said DHS declined its request, indicating that releasing the documents would “compromise national security or create other security risks.”

The Sun is appealing the denial of its FOIA request.

entries.title: Social Security Fixes Millions of Records After Trump’s Fraud Claims Fade Away
entries.summary: Trump and Musk said millions may have been receiving fraudulent benefits. Those claims were debunked, but the agency’s data cleanup continued.
entries.content:
The Social Security Administration announced Tuesday a massive overhaul to its records system, correcting death and citizenship information for nearly 15% of all active Social Security numbers.

The data cleanup — which stems from claims that millions of long-dead Americans and noncitizens may have been receiving benefit checks from the government — added 17 million missing death dates as part of an effort to modernize the agency’s antiquated bookkeeping system.

“This work represents the most comprehensive SSN record clean‑up in the agency’s 91-year history,” said a news release announcing the cleanup.

Elon Musk and President Donald Trump asserted in February 2025 that millions of people in the government’s databases were improperly getting Social Security checks — claims that were debunked when Trump’s own acting commissioner, Lee Dudek, clarified that those individuals were simply listed in historical databases without a death date and did not necessarily receive benefits.

The president has since dropped the talking point, but the data-cleaning campaign endured behind the scenes.

SSA officials did not state Tuesday whether the corrective measures stopped or reversed any improper payments, nor did they specify how much money — if any — these changes have saved the government.

The changes are also connected to the administration's fight to combat noncitizen participation in elections, which is an extremely rare occurrence. The agency said it updated 25 million records lacking citizenship details and will correct another 8.5 million records with “inaccurate citizenship status.”

Those data corrections come from the Department of Homeland Security’s Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements database. The administration recently expanded that program to incorporate SSA records to allow federal and state officials to facilitate citizenship checks before the midterms.

It is unclear whether election officials will be able to access the updated voter data just weeks ahead of the midterms, though SSA Commissioner Frank Bisignano, who was appointed in May 2025, said the records will improve fraud prevention.

“Accurate SSN records prevent fraud across federal programs and support the proper administration of benefits,” Bisignano said in Tuesday’s announcement.

In June 2025, DOGE team members copied a massive Social Security database containing the personal information of nearly every American citizen to an unapproved, third-party Cloudflare server operated entirely "outside SSA’s security protocols," according to court records.

The staffers later agreed to share voter data from that repository with a political advocacy group in an attempt to match SSA records against state voter rolls.

In a federal court filing, the SSA admitted it "doesn't know what information was shared or if it still exists on the server." The Justice Department chose not to pursue a criminal investigation into the unnamed DOGE appointees.

entries.title: Researchers Watched 3,500 Immigration Hearings. They Found a Dismantled System.
entries.summary: The way immigration courts are functioning is a facade, one of the authors of a new report said.
entries.content:
Across 13 states and thousands of cases, observers from a national court-watching initiative documented how Trump administration policies led immigration judges to quickly end cases for procedural reasons, according to a new report.

The findings from California State University, Long Beach, and Princeton University published Monday outline the mechanisms immigration courts under the Justice Department are deploying to short circuit due process. The researchers concluded deportations under this system amount to “procedural removal,” or removals based on administrative process instead of a full and fair consideration of the facts of a person’s claim to relief.

“What we see happening now is a kind of hollowing out of the content of immigration court while maintaining the facade of a judicial process,” said Princeton professor Amelia Frank-Vitale, one of the authors of the report.

Frank-Vitale and co-author Lauren Heidbrink, a professor at Cal State, Long Beach, said their report is the first of this magnitude that delves into the court processes of the second Trump administration. From January to August, researchers and university students observed nearly 3,600 hearings.

“It's not just about the outcomes, right?” Heidbrink said. “It's the process at which decisions are being made, so, in some ways, we're unmasking what those statistics actually mean.”

While the Department of Homeland Security maintains that all immigrants receive “FULL due process,” immigration judges are agreeing with the department’s attorneys to shut down cases before weighing the evidence, denials called pretermissions.

Frank-Vitale said she started noticing last summer that immigration judges were considering pretermissions at a greater scale than previous administrations. DHS is also moving to end the cases through pretermissions to send immigrants to countries they are not from, the report states.

She compared it to a criminal court where a defendant doesn’t want to take a plea deal. “It is the judge saying, ‘You know what? I'm looking at this paper filing that the cop produced, and I think you're guilty so we don't have to have a hearing,’” Frank-Vitale said.

Court observers for the report sat in on 235 hearings involving third-country removals, 90% of which happened during master calendar hearings meant for administrative functionings like scheduling. Immigration judges ordered removal of 58% of the people DHS sought to send to a country they weren’t citizens of, according to the report.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement has removed more than 25,000 people to more than 30 countries they’re not citizens of, according to the Third Country Deportation Watch. The Supreme Court last month allowed the Trump administration to carry out the third-country deportations without advance notice.

A ruling this month from the Board of Immigration Appeals upheld judges’ ability to pretermit cases without DHS attorneys asking them to do so.

Immigration judges’ compliance with DHS varies across the courts, according to the court observers. Since the start of President Donald Trump’s second term, the Justice Department has removed roughly 1 in 6 immigration judges, according to the report, replacing some with military attorneys.

Sirce Owen, the acting director of the Executive Office for Immigration Review, praised the qualifications of 47 new judges in a press release announcing their swearing in last month. “Immigration judge positions are critical to the Administration’s goal of reducing the immigration court backlog, and to restoring integrity to our immigration system,” Owen said.

Immigration judges closer to retirement were more likely to scrutinize the government’s actions because they are not afraid of getting fired, Heidbrink said.

Nearly all asylum cases are being denied as the Trump administration pushes for the judges to speed through the backlog of more than three million cases, according to data from the Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse. And former and current immigration judges previously told The Washington Sun that the administration has overhauled the system to limit their latitude.

“Again, you're narrowing the universe in which judges can judge,” Heidbrink said.
